source.title: Compressing Heavy-Tailed Weight Matrices for Non-Vacuous Generalization Bounds

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. No apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures stable rank across pretrained networks and reports classification accuracy before and after compressing final dense layers. These are related measures and interventions, rather than direct tests of the listed generalization-gap versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a stable-rank versus fitted power-law exponent relationship, and accuracy after weight-matrix compression. It does not test the listed claims about memorizing arbitrary labels, width, convolutional inductive bias, optimizer or batch choices, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples. Its cited findings are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study derives a compression-based bound, measures stable rank versus power-law exponent, and evaluates its compression method's accuracy. None tests V1–V8. Stable rank and accuracy retained after weight replacement do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps (V7). References to random-label fitting, large batches, and sharpness are background citations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they derive a compression-based generalization bound counting sparse retained parameters under i.i.d. power-law weight assumptions and report comparable accuracy after final-layer approximation. The claimed non-vacuity is theoretical; Table 1 does not numerically validate the bound. The authors acknowledge that the i.i.d. assumption is likely unrealistic for trained weights.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a theoretical matrix-compression bound and evaluates Gaussian approximation of final dense layers; it does not use the listed studies' interventions or measures of training-to-test generalization gap.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy effect varies across model and dataset; resnet20_cifar10 and resnet20_svhn show larger drops than most other listed models.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the reported pretrained final dense layers, smaller fitted power-law exponents generally cluster with smaller stable rank; no numerical association strength is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Power-law exponents of pretrained weight elements are associated with stable rank.

fits_no_version.finding: Gaussian replacement of smaller final-layer weights preserves much of the original accuracy across 12 models; ResNet-20 loses 4.71 percentage points on CIFAR-10 and 2.00 on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-layer Gaussian approximation can retain pretrained classification accuracy, with model-dependent losses.

record.problems: The generalization bound assumes i.i.d. power-law-distributed matrix elements, which the paper says is likely unrealistic for trained weights. It does not demonstrate how power-law structure arises during training. The stable-rank relationship is shown in a figure and described as general clustering, without a numerical association reported in the text. Accuracy compression experiments concern only the final dense layer of pretrained models and do not report train-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: None. The paper reports 12 model-specific accuracy comparisons in Table 1 and one aggregate stable-rank trend across 43 architectures in Figure 3; all are included.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under matched training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the contributions of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning and training recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured generalization gaps, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T6 applies relative to these eight versions. The study does not use an established version as a tool, so its evaluation of its own compression method does not warrant T4. All compression uncertainties are standard deviations across ten trials.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of the generalization gap.
Effect of removing highly memorized training examples.

rows.subject: 43 pytorch pre-trained architectures (final dense layers)
rows.operation_detail: Measured stable rank against power-law fitted exponent α across the listed pretrained architectures; spectral norm used power iteration.
rows.measure: Stable rank as a function of power-law fit exponent α; the paper reports general clustering of smaller α values with smaller stable rank, fit to a mixture of linear regressors using expectation maximization.
rows.note: The result concerns stable rank versus α, not a measured training-to-test gap.
rows.check: The reported clustering is correctly described, but stable rank versus power-law exponent measures neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor generalization gaps. Its observed state cannot apply to any listed version.

rows.operation_detail: Compressed the final dense matrix with a Gaussian approximation; repeated 10 times and averaged.

conditions.value: matrix elements less than or equal to computed standard deviation replaced with Gaussian random variables; greater elements retained

rows.note: Accuracy remained comparable after compression; this is not a train-test generalization-gap measure.
rows.check: Table 1 values and Appendix E procedure match. This evaluates the study's own compression method and should not be a claim-result row.
